steps.message:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station Egwi, Etche LGA survey stations. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 295.88 | 0.54518 | 0.54518
2 | 798.6 | 3.5924 | 4.1376
3 | 864.62 | 2.1559 | 6.2935
4 | 1810.2 | 37.957 | 37.25
5 | 5634.2 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as A-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station Egwi, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Site Report – Station Egwi, Etche LGA**

The interpreted VES model at Egwi comprises five layers with resistivities increasing progressively with depth: Layer 1 (295.88 Ωm, 0.545 m), Layer 2 (798.6 Ωm, 3.592 m), Layer 3 (864.62 Ωm, 2.156 m), Layer 4 (1810.2 Ωm, 37.957 m), and Layer 5 (5634.2 Ωm, assumed infinite/basement). Cumulative depths range from 0.545 m to approximately 42.4 m at the top of Layer 5.

Applying the curve-type notation to each consecutive triplet: Layers 1-2-3 (r1<r2<r3) → A; Layers 2-3-4 (r2<r3<r4) → A; Layers 3-4-5 (r3<r4<r5) → A. All three letters are A, consistent with a single-letter A-type curve, indicating a steadily increasing resistivity profile with depth — typical of a resistive basement underlying progressively more resistive overburden layers.

This matches the station's filed classification. No discrepancy is noted between the computed curve type and the recorded label.
